title: Sovereign SEOS handoff
description: Shared handoff envelope used by the orchestrator to pass a task to the next agent. Aligned with the framework's handoff template (revision 1, M2.2, 2026-11-11). It validates requests only; per-agent result formats are not covered (AGENT_ARCHITECTURE.md, OG-21). Format keywords such as date-time are assertions only if the validator is configured to enforce formats; the enforcement point must enable that.
$comment: Sources: framework 'Shared Handoff Schema' template; M2.2 clarification that tenant_id lives in context (declared assumption); closed objects follow the framework rule that handoffs carry a compact structured summary, not chat history. Open gaps: OG-20 (agent identifiers), OG-27 (field semantics and value sets), OG-29 (prompt version has no field).

task_id.description: Created by the orchestrator and kept for the whole chain. Format is not defined by the framework (OG-27).

parent_task_id.description: null for a root task. Relationship to the retained task_id is not defined (OG-27).

agent.description: The agent issuing this handoff. The sovereign policy only permits the orchestrator.

next_agent.description: The agent receiving this handoff. Must match the route for the action (see OPA_POLICY.rego).

action.description: What the next agent is asked to do. No value exists for the guardrail or orchestrator steps (OG-28).

priority.description: The framework template shows 'normal'; the value set is not defined (OG-27).

risk_level.description: Set by the orchestrator on every handoff.

tenant_id.description: Tenant isolation key; read by the policy as input.context.tenant_id. Declared assumption (M2.2).

payload.description: Compact structured summary of the task, never the chat history. Per-action payload shapes are not defined, so additional properties are allowed for now (OG-27).

user_request.description: Redacted or hashed request; raw text must not be carried. For the audit action the policy requires a SHA-256 hash in lowercase hex. How specialists receive the task content itself is open (OG-33).

temperature.description: The framework caps code generation at 0.3; that cap is enforced by the policy, not here.

allowed_tools.description: Must be set on every handoff; an empty list means no tools.

forbidden_actions.description: The template forbids execute_code, network_access and write_file. A side effect absent from this list counts as requested (see OPA_POLICY.rego, OG-26).

deadline.description: RFC 3339 date-time (the template uses UTC with a trailing Z). The pattern enforces the shape even when format checking is off; it does not check calendar validity. Expiry semantics are not defined (OG-27).

callback.description: Where the result is returned. The sovereign policy requires the orchestrator.
